summary.en: The account restates thresholds, rest, recurrence, merges and openness in discrete steps and whole amounts, by its own verdict restated, level or states less. It has exact thresholds for the fold's form, a periphery fold and transcritical end, per-graph threshold laws and cycle witnesses; no hysteresis loop, critical rate of a regime, escape time, chaos, self-organized criticality, percolation or dissipative structure. Of 28 entries: none carried whole, 18 in part, 4 changed, 1 history-only, 3 not carried, 2 fresh. Relations: 18 agreement, 3 scope, 3 divergence, none contrary; I looked for contrary reading and found none.

name.en: The saddle-node (fold) and the harvested equilibrium

source.work: Guckenheimer and Holmes, Nonlinear Oscillations, Dynamical Systems and Bifurcations of Vector Fields (1983); Clark, Mathematical Bioeconomics (1976); May, Nature 269 (1977)

sense.en: A stable and an unstable equilibrium meet and vanish as a parameter passes a critical value. Generically the local form is x' = r + x²: the equilibria part as the square root of the distance to the fold, and just past it a run lingers in a bottleneck whose passage time grows as the inverse square root. Under a harvest with depensation the unstable branch is a threshold level.

reading.en: The regime's `Short` and `Meets` are the sign of giving less the draw. `H + y` is the exact point between the fates and reads as the unstable branch; it is a fixed point of the step only where giving at y equals the draw, since whole-number giving can jump past it. A draw beyond all giving ends the condition from every level, which reads as past the fold. The periphery takes the fold's local form separately, as a chosen model. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (the regime; any giving law, whole numbers): where giving falls short of the draw below y, gives nothing from nothing, meets it at every z from y with z + H at most a top hi the step keeps, and 0 < H + y, a level up to hi ends exactly where it starts below H + y. The time to break lies in a band.
The margin of a regime is harvesting under depensation and the fold (Clark 1976; May 1977), in whole numbers.
Record, periphery, discrete steps: at a fold, x + h (m − x²) with rest √m, the multiplier is 1 − 2h√m; it rises to one as the margin m goes to zero, and m = ((1 − a) / (2h))².

account_adds.en: Exactness for any giving law in whole numbers; rises of joint draws superadditive up to one; and `Notch`, a witness that without giving rising with what is left no level separates the fates. S-12 asks whether this adds anything to the continuous analysis; it is unanswered.

source_adds.en: Continuous theory states that the local form is generic, with its unfolding, and the bottleneck's inverse-square-root time. Here the time band is linear in the draw less the most given, and the form is a model taken, not joined to the whole-number point. The record says the fold over the reals and the other order of a step are not stated, and yeast past its fold broke days before the constant-regime curve said.

name.en: The transcritical bifurcation and the threshold at rate one

source.work: Kermack and McKendrick (1927); Harris, The Theory of Branching Processes (1963); Diekmann, Heesterbeek and Metz, J. Math. Biol. 28 (1990)

sense.en: Two equilibria cross and exchange stability at a threshold. The zero state loses stability where a growth factor passes one, for webs where the spectral radius of a next-generation matrix does (R0). Above it a positive branch appears; a branching process at or below one dies out almost surely, except in the trivial case of exactly one offspring.

reading.en: The periphery's damped and web laws have the threshold's linear form: a + r against one, and a rate against one. The logistic drawn model has one transcritical end, its rest going to nothing as the draw reaches the renewal rate. The account does not join them, and the web law has no positive branch: past the threshold it runs away. That these are one threshold is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (periphery): with damping factor a, coupling at every step, D > 0 and a + r ≥ 0, a held loop stays bounded exactly where a + r ≤ 1. A web coupled at every step vanishes below rate one and runs away above it. At rate one, the rate does not decide whether it stays bounded.

Theorem (periphery, discrete steps, one variable linearized about a rest): at a transcritical end under a proportional draw, a rises to one as the margin shrinks. Record: under logistic renewal with a proportional draw, rest K (1 − q / r), the multiplier is 1 − h (r − q), so the stock slows in proportion to its own level.
In the model's numbers a share of none stays none (a witness): selection does not create an absent practice. So the zero state stands; the record lists a bifurcation among what it does not show.

account_adds.en: At rate one the law undecides: the identity is bounded and a shear carries 1 + n, both rate one. Stated in any normed ring.

source_adds.en: Continuous and stochastic theory states the exchange of stability as a general form, the branch where saturation bounds a web's growth, and extinction probabilities either side. Here no saturation joins the web law and no chance of extinction is stated for a branching web. 08's Loops row says the rate is not shown to be the Perron root; the record cites Gelfand's formula for the spectral radius.

name.en: Hopf bifurcation and oscillation from delay

source.work: Hopf (1942); Marsden and McCracken, The Hopf Bifurcation and Its Applications (1976); Hutchinson, Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. 50 (1948); May, Nature 261 (1976); Thomas (1981) on circuits

sense.en: As a parameter passes a value a complex pair of eigenvalues crosses into instability and a small limit cycle is born, its amplitude growing as the root of the distance, its period set by the eigenvalue (on maps, the flip and Neimark–Sacker cases). Delay in a negative loop alone can do it. Thomas's rules say which circuits oscillation and multistability need.

reading.en: No eigenvalue crossing here. What is carried is overshoot by late reading, with exact onset for one relay: past a stated bound it crosses the band and then alternates. That shares delay oscillation's mechanism, not the smooth birth of a small cycle, since a relay's swing starts at full size. `Alternation` is a period-two witness nearer the flip of overcompensating maps. Other cycles are witnesses. The relation to delay is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World; balance at the condition): with a ≤ b, 0 < a, 0 < M and the floor (ℓ + 1)M ≤ b + 1, every balanced run of a relay reading ℓ steps late, from every start below a held for its first ℓ + 1 steps, settles in the band exactly where a + (ℓ + 1)M ≤ b + 1. Record: an upward crossing is followed by a downward one and that by an upward one.

Overcompensating giving can cycle for ever (`Alternation`), a witness: giving two from nothing and nothing from more keeps a band up to two under a draw of one, yet the run from one moves between one and two at every step.
Beyond a band support can sustain a cycle (a witness): under draws of one each alone ends from every level, while from two and three the run moves between two and three and three and two for ever.

Correspondence field: the overshooting thermostat's cycle is the limit cycle of an over-compensating on-off controller. A toy rule; the record lists a heater that reads late among what it does not show.

account_adds.en: The exact whole-number onset for a late relay, and a cycle sustained by mutual support where each alone ends.

source_adds.en: Continuous theory states the crossing condition, amplitude, period and the sub- or supercritical split. 08's Loops row lists Thomas's rules and a loop's sign as not yet stated. The plan's CY(a), when an adjusted regime cycles with its period, is not built. history/SYSTEMS-COMPLEXITY-CHAOS.md reports a real delayed-feedback law, converging exactly for 0 < k < 1 and returning after six steps at k = 1: a linear crossing, off the spine.

name.en: Deterministic chaos, and what whole numbers exclude

source.work: Lorenz, J. Atmos. Sci. 20 (1963); Li and Yorke, Amer. Math. Monthly 82 (1975); May, Nature 261 (1976); Costantino and others, Science 275 (1997); Henson and others, Science 293 (2001)

sense.en: Bounded deterministic motion can be aperiodic and sensitive to its start, in very simple maps and flows, so determinism does not give long prediction from finite precision. Costantino and others report a chaotic regime in flour beetle cultures; Henson and others report lattice effects, the whole-number states pulling a chaotic model's dynamics toward cycles.

reading.en: Live laws imply a limit no live text states: within a bound a whole-number finite web's run repeats, and within a list each basin holds one cycle. That does not put chaos outside the account: the root's laws are on any type, so a shift on infinite sequences is a determined law, stated nowhere live. The records credit May (1976) for cycling only. T2's beetle test reads the Beetle Team's archive, from the group reporting these results; its text says nothing of chaos. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: It stands in theories/becoming/history/SYSTEMS-COMPLEXITY-CHAOS.md: Lorenz and May discussed, a shift map named as a Lean-proved positive witness, finite-state eventual periodicity, and no universal edge-of-chaos requirement. On the spine a reader finds no statement that sensitive dependence goes unstated, and the bound on prediction it gives is absent.

name.en: Hysteresis: distinct collapse and recovery thresholds

source.work: Noy-Meir, J. Ecol. 63 (1975); Ludwig, Jones and Holling, J. Anim. Ecol. 47 (1978); Scheffer and others, Nature 413 (2001)

sense.en: Between two folds a system has two stable states, so a parameter that drives a collapse at one value must be taken back past a different value before recovery. Which state holds depends on the path of the parameter. A loop of forward and backward thresholds is the phenomenon; the width of the band sets how costly restoration is.

reading.en: The loop is absent as a law, and the plan says so. What stands is its limit: below a need with no raising exchange a level does not return; where nothing gives nothing, an ended level stays nothing whatever the draw later does, so that branch has no recovery threshold in the draw (that composition is mine). Same level, different past, different fate is stated in the plane of level and recent giving. The records' word 'hysteresis' names memory in giving and a final ending, not this loop. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World): with balance, where the joint exchange gives no more than it takes below m, a level below m never returns to it, gated renewal being the case (`Flow.never_returns_below`).

Theorem: for giving that adjusts, rising in both and keeping a band up to hi, the runs that rest below the draw are, for each recent giving, those from levels below a least level, which does not rise as the recent giving rises. Its field frequency failed its one frozen test (MQ7: 0.39 from 5 stocks, lower bound 0.00).

With an ending made final as a separate premise, support returning after the reserve is spent finds no dependent; exhaustion alone does not give it. Its correspondence field reads 'hysteresis of collapse'.

Giving also reads what each gave last; under mutual support the order is kept; what was given can lower a threshold (`Momentum`). Its correspondence field: history-dependent response is hysteresis (Mayergoyz 2003).

A second frozen test, whether the lakes' natural renewal returns once stocking has raised their adults back above the need, is designed and refused at the agency table's header; neither frozen lake test says anything of T1.

account_adds.en: The exact premises of the one-sided case, each with a witness, and that an end absorbs while requirements do not loosen, since a dissolved requirement is transformation, not recovery. Restoration by joint net giving is a law of every balanced flow, and recovery does not guarantee maintenance.

source_adds.en: The band itself: two thresholds in a parameter, a law for the path, the width. No live law states them; the plan's CY(b) would, and its hysteresis test holds until then. Continuous theory gives the band from the two folds' positions, which the whole-number regime with a standing draw does not, a run under a changing draw not being the regime.

name.en: Tipping by rate

source.work: Wieczorek and others, Proc. R. Soc. A 467 (2011); Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 370 (2012); Scheffer and others, Ecosystems 11 (2008)

sense.en: A system can leave a state that stays stable for every frozen value of the parameter, because the parameter moves faster than a critical rate and the system cannot track it. No bifurcation need occur. Ramped past a fold slowly, by contrast, a system tips later than the static threshold, by a delay with its own scaling.

reading.en: Only a reading names this route; no law states it, as the plan records. Nearest law, on regulation: no rule reading ℓ late keeps a band unless a + 2(ℓ + 1)d ≤ b, so for a given band rests moving faster than (b − a)/(2(ℓ + 1)) cannot be held. That is a critical rate for holding a band, by my composition, not the tipping of a regime. Laws saying 'faster' or 'outruns' (a weighting against renewal, the rest's take) compare fixed rates, not a moving parameter. [AI reading]

says.en: Reading [AI, D65]: four routes of transition are distinct, none a proved phase transition: a parameter change removing a region's retention, a shock into another retained region, a failure stopping correction, and change too fast for correction.

Theorem (any type; rules over whole numbers): a rule reading ℓ steps late keeps no band [a, b] with 0 < a narrower than 2(ℓ + 1)d against rests moving the level by at most d a step, attained by the late return.

Theorem (any type): a fast difference reaches the rule only at a reading step; given two values, a stretch of L steps fixes every pair of held-rule courses with at most N states exactly when L ≥ 2N − 1. A law of reading pace, not of tipping.

Does not show that a margin times a break: yeast driven past its fold broke three and at least six days before the curve from constant regimes said. T2 (02): under a rising draw their giving falls below the curve about three days before the break (post hoc).

account_adds.en: A whole-number exact band in rate and lag, attained; and a frozen yeast run showing a renewal curve measured in constant regimes, iterated under the known schedule, did not time a break under a moving draw. The account does not read that run as rate.

source_adds.en: The critical rate of a regime; tipping from a state stable when frozen; delay past a slowly ramped fold and its scaling; pullback attractors for a moving system. A regime's draw is standing, so its theorems do not read a moving parameter. `market-finite-support-obstruction` says no R-tipping classification follows. The plan's CY(c) is not built.

name.en: Tipping by noise and escape times

source.work: Kramers, Physica 7 (1940); Freidlin and Wentzell, Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems (1984); Horsthemke and Lefever, Noise-Induced Transitions (1984)

sense.en: In a regulated state noise carries a run over a barrier. The mean time to escape grows exponentially in the barrier height over the noise strength, and a quasi-potential says which route and which state hold in the small-noise limit. Noise can also create states that the deterministic system lacks.

reading.en: What is carried is that noise leaves locks, not how long they hold. The exit law is the unregulated walk, whose Chebyshev-type bound differs in kind from an exponential residence. The closer form is a product of weights across the distance from a critical mass, a discrete relative of a barrier, in one chain of capture. That likeness to a quasi-potential is my reading; the records credit Kandori and Young. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (two values, natural weights, independent steps): the courses of n steps reaching the need take at most n·p·q/m² of the weight, Kolmogorov's maximal inequality in counting form. Reading: the unregulated case; void from n = m·m/(p·q). It is not the regime's point of no return.

Drawn one member at a time, the stag hunt leaves either lock by drift, at a weight whose bound falls across the distance from the critical mass. A time to leave a lock beyond the geometric bound is not stated.

Reading [AI, over the proved cases]: a lock read from a population drawn anew is kept for good only without noise, or where the rule leaves the disfavoured kind nothing; counts that accumulate are an urn with increasing returns (cited, not stated).
A law with noise is a relation of exchange, so the laws hold path by path; balance passes to the expectation, and rest does not (a witness).

account_adds.en: Bounds in exact counts, and a record law: given the weighting, a record bears on the exit only through the margin it shows and the steps it leaves.

source_adds.en: Continuous theory states the exponential law and its prefactor, the quasi-potential, the most likely route, and noise creating states. The record says exponential exit bounds within a horizon are not stated, nor unbalanced walks. Noise-driven exit from a regulated regime has no law; 08 lists the risk-dominant state as noise vanishes as not stated; 02's Open lists the time to leave a lock.

name.en: Absorbing-state transitions

source.work: Harris, Ann. Probab. 2 (1974); Janssen (1981); Grassberger (1982); Hinrichsen, Adv. Phys. 49 (2000)

sense.en: A nonequilibrium system with a state it cannot leave can show a sharp transition between an active and an absorbing phase as a parameter passes a critical value, with exponents shared across a universality class (directed percolation is conjectured generic). In a finite system absorption is certain eventually; sharpness belongs to the limit of infinite size.

reading.en: The account states absorption at several grains, and the premises for it, in laws that are per course and finite. It has no parameter sweep of a density and no large-size limit, so what it has is the state's closure, not the transition. A finite chain reaching its absorbing state is credited by one record, 'by hand'. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type): a configuration is drawn into some absorbing region exactly where it does not return. Near-definitional, not a classical attractor.

Theorem (World): the end absorbs: under balance, only active formations giving and activity needing support, once nothing is supported, while requirements do not loosen, nothing is supported or active again. Each premise is needed; dissolving a requirement is transformation, not recovery.
In sampled generations the ends absorb; the histories still mixed after k cohorts weigh at most r^k of (N^N)^k, finite bounds.

account_adds.en: Witnesses for each premise of absorption (a requirement dissolving, a give from beyond, an idle giver, a giver unsupported, a rise from nothing), which names what would leave the state.

source_adds.en: The transition itself: the critical parameter, order parameter, exponents and universality. All of these need densities and an infinite-size limit that the account does not represent. Its Not-shown says no universal phase threshold between regions.

name.en: Critical slowing down

source.work: Wissel, Oecologia 65 (1984); Scheffer and others, Nature 461 (2009); Dakos and others (2008, 2012)

sense.en: Near a bifurcation the rate of return to a state falls to zero, so its variance and autocorrelation rise beforehand. These can serve as generic indicators of an approaching transition, read from rolling windows of a single series.

reading.en: The periphery proves the stationary formulas of the linear step at a fixed multiplier, and that the multiplier goes to one in two chosen models, a fold's form and a logistic with a proportional draw. So the law has the field's form in a linear one-variable case. It is credited, and the record says the theory adds only the reading (see the next entry). [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (periphery; discrete steps, one variable linearized about a rest, deviation and noise independent with finite second moments): variance Var E/(1 − a²) where a² < 1, lag-1 autocorrelation a; at a fold and a transcritical end under a proportional draw, a rises to one. Nonlinear runs, finite windows and several variables are not treated.

account_adds.en: In the logistic drawn model with h, r and K nonzero a measured need's margin is read off the multiplier, with the model known (`SlowingDown.need_margin_read`).

source_adds.en: The record excludes red noise, several variables, flickering, noise-induced transitions, shifts with no bifurcation, the linearization's error near the fold and rolling-window convergence, all of which the field treats. Continuous-time diffusion forms are also unstated.

name.en: How far early warnings reach

source.work: Scheffer and others, Nature 461 (2009), on generic signals; Boerlijst, Oudman and de Roos (2013); Dekker, von der Heydt and Dijkstra (2018); Hastings and Wysham, Ecol. Lett. 13 (2010)

sense.en: The field's general reading is that rising variance and autocorrelation warn of a coming critical transition across many systems. Later work in the field qualifies this: a warning shows only in what carries the critical mode, a leading system's indicators may ignore whether a follower tips, and shifts can come with no warning at all.

reading.en: T6 confines the signal: the statistic reads the observed condition's own rate of return, and a dependent's need is no bifurcation of that renewal. The confinement is the later literature's too: the audit says the uncoupled side holds by construction in matched form and is the eigenvector literature's, and the chapter says that literature refuted T6's first wording. So this is scope with no third part. Its empirical content, negligible feedback, no test has measured. [AI reading]

says.en: Thesis T6: a break is seen coming only through what couples into what breaks. The invisible half proved on the World model; the seen half periphery; one law across domains, and 'only where' outside these models, conjectured. Three frozen seabird tests did not reject it at their thresholds; none establishes conditional independence.

Theorem (World): where that stock is the only requirement that may fail up to a horizon, some raise of it is alike through the couplings and supports the formation to the horizon: how far off the break is does not couple in.
Audit: 'the uncoupled side holds by construction in matched form and is the eigenvector literature's'. Dekker and others (2018) named as the closest prior form of the uncoupled side.

Theorem (World: balance; nothing given): where each step's draw exceeds everything drawn since T, more than half of what stood at T stands at each of those steps; a stock of seven meets draws of one, two and four, four standing at the third step and none after. A witness of no warning in the level, by a growing draw.
Up to T the carried amount reads only couplings acting before T; a loop forming at T and one forming at any later step carry the same amounts up to T (`Closing.Onset.unforeseen`, a witness).

account_adds.en: The split stated as one thesis with a forbidden observation fixed in advance. 08 records that prose once said nothing sensed shows how near a break is, and corrects it: the theorem assumes the stock is not sensed.

source_adds.en: Hastings and Wysham's shifts with no warning under strong noise or chaos: the account's no-warning laws are other mechanisms, and the record lists shifts with no bifurcation as not shown. Whether T6 says anything beyond the case without feedback is S-16's open question.

name.en: Self-organized criticality

source.work: Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld, Phys. Rev. Lett. 59 (1987); Dhar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64 (1990)

sense.en: A slowly driven threshold system with fast relaxation tunes itself, with no external parameter, to a critical state where responses come as avalanches of all sizes, in power-law distribution. The sandpile's abelian property says the order of topplings does not change the result. How widely real systems are so is disputed.

reading.en: Whole numbers are no obstacle: the sandpile is in whole grains. The neighbours are chip-firing's termination, credited, its order independence listed as not stated, and a cascade along chains of total dependence. I found nothing stating slow drive with fast relaxation, a self-tuned margin or a size law. The regime's draw is standing, so its margin does not tune itself. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: All of it: the self-tuning, the avalanche distribution, the abelian group. 08's table names only chip-firing's order independence and thresholds in chips as stated elsewhere. My remark: a stock self-tuned near its need would bear on T1 and T6; this is unexplored.

name.en: Highly optimized tolerance: robust yet fragile

source.work: Carlson and Doyle, Phys. Rev. E 60 (1999); Phys. Rev. Lett. 84 (2000)

sense.en: Against self-organized criticality, power laws can come from design or selection optimizing under constraints: a system tuned against the perturbations it was designed for grows robust to them and fragile to rare or unanticipated ones.

reading.en: Proposed here, not in the account, and only for HOT's 'unanticipated' half: what an optimizing order does not read takes the shared constraint's cost. With room, every optimum stands at the least level beyond. Fragility to rare events differs: HOT's design reads their probability and weighs them low, which this law does not state. HOT's tail law has no counterpart. Standing: my reading only. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any set of outcomes; the breaks on the World): with room every optimum of an order rising with a family stands at the least level beyond, and, on a web with each condition beyond depended on at a need met at the step, breaks exactly the dependences beyond that some eligible outcome breaks.

account_adds.en: Exact conditions for the drain, room and the outcome set, on one step, for every order rising with the family; 08 says the law restates Zhuang and Hadfield-Menell's Theorem 1. No evaluation enters: the record says the beyond's fall is not shown a harm.

source_adds.en: The trade-off curve and tail distributions from a design problem. No statement here says how losses are distributed by size, and no optimum here is measured on an event distribution.

name.en: Percolation: a sharp threshold over an ensemble of webs

source.work: Broadbent and Hammersley (1957); Erdős and Rényi (1960); Callaway and others, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85 (2000)

sense.en: On a large random or lattice web a connected cluster spanning the system appears sharply at a threshold in the share of links or nodes kept. Removing nodes past it fragments the web, the threshold depending on the degree distribution. Sharpness belongs to the limit of large size.

reading.en: The neighbours are per graph and exact, not statistical over an ensemble: a set relying on at most its tolerance outside it keeps giving; a cascade down chains of total dependence; points of no return not rising under mutual support. None gives a threshold in a share of links or a cluster's size. The next two entries take what per-graph form there is; the plan's 'percolation-like' tolerance gap names this. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: The sharp threshold, its dependence on degree distribution, size scaling and the giant component. No law here reads an ensemble of webs. Plan 4.4 lists thresholds of tolerance on webs as a gap; what 05 states is per graph, a kept set and monotonicity.

name.en: Threshold contagion on a given graph

source.work: Granovetter, Am. J. Sociol. 83 (1978); Chalupa, Leath and Reich, J. Phys. C 12 (1979); Morris, Rev. Econ. Stud. 67 (2000); Watts, PNAS 99 (2002)

sense.en: A node adopts once enough of its neighbours have. Thresholds rising or falling move the outcome monotonically. On a given graph contagion from a seed stops at a sufficiently cohesive set (Morris, in fractions); on random graphs a global cascade appears within a window of connectivity and thresholds (Watts).

reading.en: Proposed here: the tolerating law is a threshold model on a given graph of waits, written by tolerance rather than need. `kept_set` has the form of a cohesive set blocking contagion, and a thin withholding that passes out in one step the form of a seed too thin to spread. The record credits none of this literature and reads onto social viability; the link is mine. No law says whether a seed spreads globally. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type; the web reading on the World): under the tolerating law a formation gives where all but its tolerance of what it waits on gave. A set giving at the start, each member waiting on at most its tolerance outside it, keeps giving whatever the rest does, and a thin withholding passes out in one step. In a triad one withholding spreads to all with tolerance zero and passes out with tolerance one.

Theorem (any type): for the same waits and start, a formation giving under a tolerating law gives under every tolerating law with tolerances no smaller. It shows only that more tolerance gives no less, not that it is better. Correspondence field: monotone threshold dynamics.

account_adds.en: From total withholding, restoring needs a formation sparing all it waits on, and without one total withholding stays; on a gift web support is a run of the law, with tolerance the number upstream less the need.

source_adds.en: The global cascade window, degree distributions, fractions of neighbours and any ensemble. The record excludes amounts of giving, thresholds with memory and how tolerances form.

name.en: Cascades along dependence and interdependent networks

source.work: Pimm (1980); Dunne, Williams and Martinez (2002); Buldyrev and others, Nature 464 (2010)

sense.en: Failure passes along dependence. In food webs the reach of secondary extinctions is set by the web's structure. In two interdependent networks a cascade of mutual dependence can fragment both abruptly, leaving them more fragile than either alone.

reading.en: The chain law has the deterministic form: along total dependence with positive draws the end of one ends everything downstream, a ring together or not at all, and a draw of nothing stops it; a reserve defers it link by link. Buldyrev's abruptness is a statistic of random graphs, absent here. The records credit the food-web work, not Buldyrev; that resemblance is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (the regime; any number of conditions, any index type): under mutual support raising a level never ends one that held; along every chain of total dependence with positive draws the end of one ends everything downstream, a ring ending together or not at all, and a draw of nothing stops the cascade.

Theorem (World): where the reserve decays, along a chain of embodied links, each requiring the one before at a positive need from T on with the first ended from T, coextinction runs down the chain link by link; without decay each link ends given excluded middle, with no bound.

account_adds.en: Each link's steps counted, positive draws shown needed by a witness, and a calibration: naming when a deferred end comes is an omniscience principle.

source_adds.en: Partial dependence and a cascade's time, which 02's Open lists; reach as a statistic of web structure, the record calling field reach untested; abrupt collapse under random failure and its threshold.

name.en: Open systems: order kept by what flows through

source.work: Schrödinger, What Is Life? (1944); Nicolis and Prigogine, Self-Organization in Nonequilibrium Systems (1977)
source.locator: the entropy balance dS = d_e S + d_i S; locator unverified

sense.en: A system stays away from equilibrium only by exchange with its surroundings: its internal entropy production is non-negative, and the balance is kept by entropy exported, or free energy taken in, at rates the theory quantifies.

reading.en: The necessity is the account's, in amounts: an enclosed finite family taken from without end cannot go unfed from beyond. It is one direction, and openness does not suffice for arising without end. The audit says the exclusion is the sources' own and the theory forbids no more and needs more to forbid it. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World; balance and dissipation, equality of conditions decided): a finite family without repetition, enclosed around from some step on and taken from or rising at arbitrarily late steps, cannot from any step on be fed from nothing beyond it. No step of feeding is named. It needs a fixed unit of natural-number amounts.
The eight premises decide neither enclosure nor openness, and openness with them does not give arising without end.
Fed from beyond, entropy, nets: restated; closest prior Schrödinger (1944), Prigogine (1977), ranking functions, P-invariants.

account_adds.en: The premises needed, each with a witness (censuses, embodiment), and calibration at the unit: at a unit that splits at arbitrarily late steps the conclusion can fail.

source_adds.en: Rates and amounts: S-06 says the law gives no amount, rate or time of feeding, which an entropy-production balance would give. No theorem states the law over real amounts.

name.en: Dissipative structures and least entropy production

source.work: Glansdorff and Prigogine, Thermodynamic Theory of Structure, Stability and Fluctuations (1971); Nicolis and Prigogine (1977); Bénard cells, Belousov–Zhabotinsky as examples

sense.en: Near equilibrium, in the linear regime, a steady state minimizes entropy production. Far from equilibrium that steady state can lose stability at a bifurcation, and new ordered patterns form and are kept by dissipation itself: order through fluctuation. The near-equilibrium principle's reach has been contested (uncertain in detail).

reading.en: The account states that continuing needs feeding, not that a throughput forms structure; I found no law where a homogeneous steady state loses stability. 08 itself lists both as stated by prior frameworks and not yet here. Were they taken up, the account would still refuse one reading: the glossary says neither its generation nor 生生 is any new organization, so a Bénard cell's order would say nothing of direction. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: All of it: the extremum principle, the bifurcation, pattern forming, and the temperature and force gradients that a level in whole units of exergy against one reference environment does not represent. Stated limit: 08's last column of the Fed from beyond row.

name.en: Landauer's principle and Bennett's history

source.work: Landauer, IBM J. Res. Dev. 5 (1961); Bennett, IBM J. Res. Dev. 17 (1973); Sagawa (2014)

sense.en: A logically irreversible step compresses the phase space of the bearer of information, so under Liouville's theorem the rest expands, and erasing a bit at temperature T exports at least kT ln 2 of heat in expectation. Keeping a history makes computation logically reversible; Bennett's uncomputation returns the history to blank.

reading.en: The count is carried for determined maps on listed configurations. The account reads that one merge across computation, heat, extinction and forgetting, as correspondence. It also corrects its own earlier use: the heat bound is no floor of destroyed exergy, so it does not supply the World's least loss. Physics enters only through a stated count-to-heat premise. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type; a law that merges nothing): a part reset at every step means no list holds every configuration. 'This is Landauer's (1961) count with Bennett's (1973) history'; no energy, temperature or probability is read, so kT ln 2 is not derived.

Landauer's bound is no such floor by itself: it bounds the heat an erasure exports, heat exported is not exergy destroyed, and a logically irreversible step can be carried out thermodynamically reversibly (Bennett 2003; Sagawa 2014).

account_adds.en: The law at any type: a reset part under a law that merges nothing means no list holds the configurations; narrowing the part spreads the rest. The record reads the finite-rest floor as the counting shadow of Reeb and Wolf's finite-bath correction.

source_adds.en: The bound in energy, kT ln 2; the physics of the bath and of measure on phase space, since a list has no measure. Bennett's uncomputation (only the kept history is stated). 08's table lists both as not yet stated.

name.en: The attractor of dynamical systems

source.work: Milnor, Commun. Math. Phys. 99 (1985); Conley, Isolated Invariant Sets and the Morse Index (1978)

sense.en: An attractor is an invariant set, minimal in some sense, attracting a neighbourhood or a set of positive measure; the definition needs a topology or a measure. Conley's theorem splits a flow on a compact space into a chain-recurrent part and a gradient-like part.

reading.en: The account uses a different object and says so: absorbing region, drawn into it, with no neighbourhood, measure, or minimality. So the main law is near-definitional, 'drawn exactly where it does not return'; its record is explicit that this is no attractor in the classical sense. A topology-free shadow of Conley's split seems near; that is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type): a configuration is drawn into some absorbing region exactly where it does not return. 'The main law is near-definitional, not a classical attractor'. Record: how deep or wide a basin is lies outside the theorems.
Theorem (any type): courses meeting is an equivalence whose classes are basins; within m listed configurations each basin holds one cycle.

account_adds.en: No finiteness or decidability is needed for the main law; an open world can draw without merging, while within a list the two go together. The periphery's market model does use neighbourhood attraction at one parameter: at β = 1/2 the maintenance end and the depletion end each attract a neighbourhood.

source_adds.en: Stability under nearby starts, basin size and shape, strange attractors, and fractal basin boundaries. The word 'attractor' on the spine therefore does not promise these, and a physicist reading the account's 'attractor' as Milnor's would be misled unless told.

name.en: Bistability, basin boundaries and transients

source.work: Hirsch and Smith, Monotone Dynamical Systems (2005); Hastings, Trends Ecol. Evol. 19 (2004); Dean, Am. Nat. 121 (1983)

sense.en: Two stable states are separated by a boundary, in the plane a curve, unordered for order-preserving maps. Which state a run reaches depends on its start; basins have sizes, and transients can cross what a lower-dimensional view takes for a threshold. In obligate mutualism a curve separates persistence from extinction.

reading.en: The account states the boundary exactly where the order holds: a least level for each recent giving, a falling curve; a partner's threshold not rising as the partner rises. The stag hunt's critical mass is the same shape in shares, where without noise the start decides, and the market has two attracting ends at one parameter. Basin sizes it does not state. A shared shape, read across models; the account does not join them. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem: for giving rising in what is left and the recent giving and keeping a band up to hi, the runs resting below the draw are, for each recent giving, those from levels below a least level, decided at step 3 hi + 3, not rising as the recent giving rises. Without rising giving no level separates the fates (`Notch`, a witness).

The point decides the fate where the recent giving lies on the level's side; otherwise what was given can carry a condition across it (`Crossing.crosses`, a witness). Its correspondence field: with a second state variable a threshold is a curve that transients cross (Hastings 2004).
Under mutual support within a band a run rests and a point of no return does not rise as the partner rises; support can save, and inhibition breaks the order of fates.

Theorem (periphery): at β = 1/2 the maintenance end and the depletion end each attract a neighbourhood, and the interior point has arbitrarily small perturbations that leave. Record: no full basin, and no stability classification for every β.

account_adds.en: Exact premises with witnesses, the boundary found by a finite search with no omniscience, and an inhibition witness where the threshold rises with the partner, so that down-closure is seen to rest on mutual support.

source_adds.en: Basin size and shape, separatrices as manifolds, and laws of how long transients last. Over the reals the threshold as a computed level is not stated. In the field the curve's fates failed their frozen test (MQ7: 0.39 from 5 stocks, lower bound 0.00), so its use on data is not established.

name.en: Monotone dynamical systems

source.work: Hirsch (1985); Smith, Monotone Dynamical Systems (1995); Hirsch and Smith (2005)

sense.en: Where each component's rate rises with the others, the order of solutions is kept. Strongly monotone flows converge for generic starts and their limit sets are unordered; planar cooperative flows converge outright. Competitive maps keep the order with one coordinate reversed. Delays can be absorbed into the state.

reading.en: Mutual support is the cooperative premise, and the records credit the comparison principle. Discrete steps part here: beyond a band a pair under mutual support cycles for ever between two unordered states, which the unordered-limit-set result allows and which a planar cooperative flow, in my comparison, does not do. So the band is what rest needs in whole steps. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (the regime; finitely many listed conditions, band, mutual support): a run rests within the count times hi plus one steps, ending decided there, and each point of no return, the others given, is exact and does not rise as any other level rises.

Record counterexample `Relay.cycles`: mutual support without a band gives no rest; a pair each of which ends alone cycles for ever between two unordered states. Correspondence field: planar cooperative maps are eventually monotone only under regularity conditions (Smith 1998).

The order, the shape of a run and its rests hold in linearly ordered amounts. Theorem (periphery): over the non-negative reals, with the adjustment rising in what is left and in the recent giving and keeping a band up to hi, every run converges, to a rest where the adjustment is continuous, and need not rest.

account_adds.en: The record says the shape of a run needs no regularity condition here, since every step neither up nor down moves the recent giving toward the draw, whatever the adjustment; stated constructively in any amounts, with convergence left to the periphery as an omniscience principle.

source_adds.en: Generic convergence in continuous time, the strong order, and systems with delay beyond one recent giving. A further lag is not stated, and that measured adjustments rise in both over their band is not shown.

name.en: Viability and invariance kernels

source.work: Aubin, Viability Theory (1991)

sense.en: Under a set-valued dynamic, a set is viable if from each state some evolution stays in it, and invariant if every evolution does. Within a constraint the largest such sets are the viability and invariance kernels. In continuous time a tangency condition characterizes them; in discrete time a fixed-point iteration computes them.

reading.en: The 'never leaving' law has this form, for every process and guard: no course leaves exactly when a certificate inside the guard, kept by every step, contains the start. A record corrected the name to invariance kernel, the two coinciding for a determined law. Whole steps and any type, so no tangency arises. The market's floors are supplied, and its kernel is not computed. [AI reading]

says.en: Never leaving. For every process and guard, no course from a configuration leaves the guard exactly when some certificate contains it (a set within the guard that every step keeps; the invariance kernel is the largest). Scope: no entry from unsafe states, no compliance by actual markets.

Reaching. A start reaches a target within n steps on every admissible disturbance exactly when some funnel holds it at level n; in the market every such state lands exactly when β ≤ 5/12. Not a complete basin or a measured threshold; the record says no bifurcation over all parameters follows.

account_adds.en: Reaching and lasting as the same kind of ladder (funnels, ladders, drains), as pure-core laws for any process, with market instances in the periphery.

source_adds.en: Tangency conditions, set-valued continuous dynamics, regularity of kernels, and viable control synthesis. The record says the market's kernel, the complete region of nonfailure, is not computed.

name.en: Phase transitions in statistical physics

source.work: Landau (1937); Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65 (1944); Yang and Lee, Phys. Rev. 87 (1952); Wilson (1971)

sense.en: A phase transition is a singularity in thermodynamic quantities in the infinite-size limit, described by an order parameter, with scaling and universality explained by renormalization. A finite system of the usual kind has no true singularity, by Yang and Lee.

reading.en: The home text refuses the word: thresholds here are exact points in finite whole-number models, not singularities in a limit. Yet records' correspondence fields keep a line of Ren's calling 'not harm' 'a phase transition with a clear boundary' and one calls three laws 'phase results', AI-read. A reader of a record could take those as the physicist's sense. I flag it. [AI reading]

says.en: Reading [AI, D65]: a region ceasing, a state's departure and a strict bifurcation are not one 'phase transition'. Not shown: 'no universal phase threshold between regions'.
Reading [AI, D65]: four routes of transition are distinct, none a proved phase transition.

Correspondence: Ren said that 'not harm' is 'a phase transition with a clear boundary'; the two earlier phase results and this absorbing end are its three forms under this reading. The reading and the names are the AI's.

account_adds.en: One law of exact thresholds for any fate down-closed in the level and read off an exact check, which has no need of a limit.

source_adds.en: The limit, the order parameter, exponents, universality classes, renormalization. `losses-of-the-sum-over-histories` says only that renormalization of its sum is not stated. No live text compares the lumping laws (S-23) with a renormalization flow; I searched for the word and did not study the likeness.

name.en: Stability theory: rates, linearization, asymptotics

source.work: Lyapunov (1892); Hartman (1960) and Grobman (1959); LaSalle, The Stability of Dynamical Systems (1976)

sense.en: Near a hyperbolic equilibrium a nonlinear flow is conjugate to its linear part, whose eigenvalues classify the state and give exponential rates. A Lyapunov function proves stability, the invariance principle says where runs go, and convergence may be asymptotic, never arriving.

reading.en: The ranking argument is carried, and whole numbers change the question most here: with a least loss a run arrives, so convergence becomes rest in finitely many steps, bounding how many falls, not when. Without a least loss a closed amount still approaches rest, which is the asymptotic case. Over the reals the periphery states only a band's monotone convergence and damped and web thresholds. The eigenvalue is present once, a multiplier in slowing down. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem: over any amounts, an amount not rising from T on, falling by at least ε at each step at which P holds, with m copies of ε not within its value at T, has steps at which P holds not recurring. Halving stocks never rest. Over finitely many configurations a loss above nothing needs a law that merges.

Theorem (periphery): over the non-negative reals, with the adjustment rising in what is left and in the recent giving and keeping a band up to hi, every run starting with both within hi converges, to a rest where the adjustment is continuous, and need not rest.

Rest needs a least loss: restated. Not yet: stability in continuous time, exponential or asymptotic rates and LaSalle's largest invariant set (here discrete rest, bounding how many falls and not when rest comes, with the discrete invariance principle).

account_adds.en: The cost named as a theorem: no reading into whole numbers keeps the falls of an amount falling at every step. And constructive calibration: naming when rest comes is an omniscience principle.

source_adds.en: Linearization and its eigenvalue classification, exponential and asymptotic rates, converse Lyapunov theorems, continuous time, and a basin estimated from a Lyapunov level. 02's Open lists real amounts, damping strengths and continuous time.

name.en: Continuous time and real amounts against steps and units

source.work: Poincaré–Bendixson theorem, as in Hirsch, Smale and Devaney, Differential Equations, Dynamical Systems and an Introduction to Chaos (2004); Mollison (1991) on the atto-fox

sense.en: An autonomous flow on a line cannot oscillate and one in the plane cannot be chaotic; a discretized flow can show cycles its flow lacks, and samples can hide what happens between them. A continuous stock only tends to zero, and can recover from arbitrarily little, a known artifact of such models for populations.

reading.en: 08 names the cost of steps and units: real-time balance samples exactly, yet a course can stand still at every instant and change between. No live text draws two further results, which I draw here. One condition's `Alternation` is a step's overshoot, which a flow on a line cannot do, so it needs a delay or a stage before it is read on a continuous system. And a whole-number level below its point is nothing in finitely many steps, where a continuous stock never arrives. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (periphery): a course in real time balances across every step of any reading at instants, but a balanced course can stand still at every whole instant and change between them. No reading into whole numbers keeps the falls of an amount falling at every step. It does not show that actual rates are summable or that amounts are real, nor that the whole-number laws fail where they apply.

Record law: where giving falls short of the draw below y and nothing gives from nothing, a positive level below H + y falls at every step, is nothing after as many steps as it stood, and stays nothing. The other order of a step (giving before the draw) is not stated.
Open: real amounts, damping strengths, continuous time, infinitely many conditions; the regime's threshold over the reals as a computed level.

account_adds.en: The whole-number forms hold over any amounts with a least fall or a least separation, so the commitment is to a least change, not to whole numbers as such; and a rest theorem read off listed configurations needs no least loss.

source_adds.en: Flows, rates and time-scale separation, and everything that depends on them: the fold, transcritical and rate laws above in continuous form, and how a step's size moves a law. S-12 asks whether the other order of a step would move the point of no return. Whether a law survives refinement of the step is not stated.

name.en: The arrow: entropy rising in an isolated system

source.work: Clausius (1865); Boltzmann (1877); Zermelo (1896) and Loschmidt (1876) as objections; Lebowitz, Physics Today 46 (1993)

sense.en: An isolated system's entropy does not fall, and in Boltzmann's reading it rises because macrostates with more microstates are far more numerous, given an ordered start. Reversibility and recurrence object, and the usual answer rests on a premise about the start and on long recurrence times.

reading.en: The objections are carried: within listed configurations a quantity rising along an orbit rules out a law that merges nothing, which the record reads as Zermelo's and Loschmidt's. So a universal rise is scoped: an arrow needs a merge or room no list holds. What rises with no premise here is the history of exchanges, not a state function, and 'entropy' naming the record is a reading, not the same reference. The second law enters the periphery as a premise. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World): with no premise a family's history of exchanges never shrinks; under balance, the family gaining nothing from T on, an arrow from T leaves change not recurring. Record: a coarse-grained entropy rising from an ordered start needs a premise about the start and is not stated. 'The correspondences to thermodynamics are readings, not physical derivations.'

Theorem (any type): within finitely many configurations, a list holding every one, a determined law merges nothing exactly where every configuration returns; a quantity that never falls along an orbit and rises at some step of it rules out a law that merges nothing.
Theorem (periphery): under the exergy balance and the second law nothing comes from nothing at the unit; the second law alone gives no dissipation. Physics enters by stated correspondence.

account_adds.en: As laws, in double-negation form where stated: on the family's listed configurations, an arrow or dissipation rules out a law merging nothing. And the second law read in available work gives the spine's first law; no converse is proved.

source_adds.en: The statistical account of the rise: coarse-graining, typicality of macrostates, the past hypothesis, recurrence times. S-04 warns the name 'first law' for `Flow.Gainless` may mislead physicists, since the second law gives it.

name.en: Morphogenesis: instability of a homogeneous state

source.work: Turing, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237 (1952); Curie (1894)

sense.en: Reaction and diffusion, each stabilizing alone, can together destabilize a uniform state, and small disturbances grow into a pattern with a selected wavelength. Turing notes the uniform state needs disturbances to leave; instability thus takes part in formation.

reading.en: Only the obstruction is carried: a symmetric law from a symmetric start keeps the symmetry, and noise of one law keeps it in distribution. That is Curie's side, Turing's remark, not his mechanism. No account of space, diffusion, or a homogeneous state losing stability exists on the spine. The live use is against guarantees in the free-energy literature. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type of cell states and fields): under a descent moving every cell by one rule, from its own state and a field read from the configuration, never from a cell's number, two cells alike at the start are alike at every step.

Over finite states, an exchangeable start stays exchangeable under noise of one law at every cell; independent noise can part identical cells but never with certainty. Densities, continuous states or time, and Langevin flows are not stated.

account_adds.en: The obstruction in exact finite form, in free-energy terms, with what breaks it named: a start that differs, a rule reading a cell's number, or noise.

source_adds.en: The dispersion relation, wavelength selection, the condition on diffusivities, pattern in space. The account has no continuous space, and the history page names Turing's analysis, which live text cites only for its remark on disturbances.

name.en: Complexity as a direction: order for free, the edge of chaos

source.work: Kauffman, The Origins of Order (1993) and Investigations (2000); Langton, Physica D 42 (1990); Chaisson, Cosmic Evolution (2001)

sense.en: Some complexity writers hold that order arises spontaneously, that life sits near an edge of chaos (Langton, Kauffman; contested), that a biosphere tends to enter its adjacent possible as fast as it can sustain (Kauffman, tentative), or that complexity rises with energy rate density (Chaisson). Attributions from memory, compressed; each author's claim differs in strength.

reading.en: The account finds no direction in the dynamics. A part can go on while closing what lies beyond its dependence, so persistence does not select widening, and 'reality develops more responsive renewal' forbids nothing measurable as stated. No dynamic is good or bad here. Ranking courses needs C for order, and whose losses count the continuation condition for scope; neither is asserted and their warrant is open. Kauffman's law, read on the pasts, loses all precedence at its widest course. [AI reading]

says.en: Not shown: that generation is better than keeping or degeneration: order needs C, whose losses count needs the continuation condition. Nor that the regions are decided at a point, or that renewal is generation.

An empirical target, not a premise: that reality generally develops more shared and more responsive renewal forbids nothing measurable as stated. A part can go on while closing what lies beyond its dependence (`Clearing.loses_beyond`), so persistence alone does not select widening; over which runs, or how fast, it should hold is unsaid.
Reading after the law: Kauffman's tentative law, read on the pasts, has its widest course lose all precedence; read on kinds of birth the extremes are incomparable at offset 2.
The possible within a horizon restates Kauffman's adjacent possible (2000) for a prestated space, not the one that cannot be prestated (Longo, Montévil and Kauffman 2012).

account_adds.en: Witnesses and exact premises against reading persistence as direction, and the separation of the direction's warrant from any dynamics.

source_adds.en: Empirical measures and trends of complexity and rate density, and random Boolean networks. None is taken up. The edge of chaos stands only in history/SYSTEMS-COMPLEXITY-CHAOS.md, which says there is no established universal requirement that learning or life occupy one.
